job: My mother lives alone and can't bend down any more. The TV remote is on the low footstool by her bed and there is a towel on the edge of the bath, please pick both up. Fetch her pill organiser from the kitchen counter and wipe her bedside table.

world.source: hand-written scenario, not a scan: a one-bedroom apartment for an older resident, with a narrow bathroom door

output.understood_as: For a mother who can no longer bend down, pick up the TV remote from the low footstool by her bed and the towel from the bath edge, fetch her pill organiser from the kitchen counter, and wipe her bedside table.
steps: In the bedroom, pick up the TV remote from the low footstool.
Wipe the bedside table with a cloth.
In the bathroom, pick up the towel from the edge of the bath.
In the kitchen, pick up the pill organiser from the counter.
Nothing is carried out of the building.

tasks.why: She cannot bend down to reach the remote on the low footstool.
The job asks for her bedside table to be wiped, and it is in the same room as the remote.
The towel on the bath edge is too low for her to reach.
The job asks for her pill organiser to be fetched from the kitchen counter.

demos.why: Shows how a hand reaches down to the low footstool and lifts the remote off it.
The remote is smooth and can slip, and pressing too hard could press its buttons.
Shows the wiping strokes across the bedside table, going around anything standing on it.
Sets how firmly to hold the cloth so it does not slip out of the hand while pressing on the table.
Shows how to take the towel off the bath edge without dragging it into the bath.
A soft towel can slip out of a weak grip or drop part of itself.
Shows how to lift the organiser off the counter and keep it level.
Squeezing too hard can pop the lids open and spill the pills, and gripping too lightly can drop it.

questions: Where should the remote, the towel and the pill organiser go once they are picked up? For example, should the remote and the pill organiser go on her bedside table and the towel on a rail? The robot can only take things to the way out at the moment, so please tell us the exact places.
The only towel card we have is a hand towel bunched on the floor. Is the towel on the bath edge a small hand towel, or a larger bath towel? If it is a bath towel, roughly how heavy is it?
Should anything be cleared off the bedside table before it is wiped, and should it be put back afterwards?
unmet: Handing things to your mother or putting them where she can reach them (remote and pill organiser by her, towel hung up) is not covered. The robot can pick them up, but it can only route items to the way out, not to a spot in the flat.
Bringing the pill organiser from the kitchen to her is not covered. The robot will pick it up, but it cannot yet carry it to her bedroom.
